stem:
Farhan sees water vapour rise on a warm afternoon. High in the air it cools and forms white clouds. Later rain falls; his book also names hail and snow.

Which statement best describes how water vapour becomes clouds and then rain, hail, or snow?

options.text: Water vapour rises, cools, and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds; many droplets together can fall as rain, hail, or snow.
Clouds are made of water vapour, not liquid water droplets.
Every cloud produces rain as soon as its tiny droplets form.
A cloud starts raining when it turns dark.

teacher.key_rationale: Water vapour rises, cools, and condenses into tiny liquid droplets that form clouds; many droplets can fall as rain, hail, or snow. Clouds are not uncondensed vapour alone. Not every cloud rains at once. Darkness alone does not start rain.
